hypotheses.mechanism: Faster filing availability may identify operational reporting discipline without using market returns.
hypotheses.primaryClaim: Pre-2021 SEC registrants with consistently shorter accepted-at filing lags show higher subsequent filing continuity than otherwise comparable registrants.
hypotheses.falsificationCriterion: The preregistered interval for the lag-stratified continuity difference includes no practically positive effect or points negative.

hypotheses.mechanism: An amendment-free filing path may proxy reporting-process stability.
hypotheses.primaryClaim: Pre-2021 registrants without later amendments in the frozen observation window show higher subsequent standard-concept ascertainment.
hypotheses.falsificationCriterion: The preregistered ascertainment difference is not positive after frozen missingness rules.

hypotheses.mechanism: Identity and action missingness may cluster by exchange, era, size proxy and terminal event class, creating non-random survivorship exposure.
hypotheses.primaryClaim: The pre-2021 probability of an unresolved identity or terminal-wealth cell differs materially across frozen source-era and event-class strata.
hypotheses.falsificationCriterion: All preregistered stratum contrasts remain below the practical heterogeneity threshold after multiplicity control.

hypotheses.mechanism: Terminal-wealth omission can distort retrospective conclusions even when last-session prices agree across vendors.
hypotheses.primaryClaim: In a separately sealed pre-2021 terminal-event cohort, inference categories change when documented post-session payments and recoveries are included instead of last-session value alone.
hypotheses.falsificationCriterion: No preregistered inference category changes and the sensitivity interval stays below the practical threshold.
